115	stage, to skip one, or to stop early. The only things that change how the
116	next stage is posed are the ones `PROTOCOL.md` names: *budget*, *error*,
117	and (`QUESTIONS.md`, Q7) *timeout*. P13's rule that larger n are not run
118	after a limit stop is applied by whoever runs the batch, across runs, not
119	by `run` (Q10).
120	
121	## 4. The operations
122	
123	These are `PROTOCOL.md`'s, made concrete. A per-system harness implements
124	exactly these and nothing that orders, chooses or re-poses goals on its
125	own.
126	
127	### pose(stage)
128	
129	Gives the system the information of stage k, in one of two ways, chosen
130	by the configuration's systems file ("The same computation"), never by
131	the harness from results:
132	
133	- **incremental**: stage k is received into the computation that holds
134	  stages 1 to k−1 (an Absys session, a SWI-Prolog *session* engine, a
135	  Python or ALGOL 60 program that reads each stage from its input as it
136	  arrives). Recorded `posed.how = "incremental"`.
137	- **reposed**: a new computation is started, and stages 1 to k are
138	  replayed into it **in order, every one of them, replacements and
139	  withdrawals included** (P10, P15d). The program carries them out. The
140	  harness never works out the net information itself, never drops a
141	  stage that a later one replaced or withdrew, and never merges stages.
142	  Recorded `posed.how = "reposed"`, `posed.replayed = [1, …, k−1]`.
143	
144	Stage 1 is always `fresh`. What the harness gives the program is only:
145	which stage to pose (k), for a reposed run the list of stages to replay
146	(1 … k−1) and any replayed commitments (below), and the instance's
147	parameters (n, order, answer mode, as `stages.json` gives them). The
148	program holds the stage information. The harness never passes a constant
149	of a problem.
150	
151	**No anticipation** (`PROTOCOL.md`, "Writing a program", rule 5): the
152	harness tells the program about stage k only when stage k is posed, and
153	never tells it how many stages follow.
154	
155	### spawn(computation)
156	
157	P09a, P09b and P16b. Starts a separate computation **in the same
158	instance of the system**, sharing one database, never in a separate
159	operating system process (`PROTOCOL.md`). `stages.json` lists the
160	computations a stage spawns (`spawns`) and, for P09a, the order
161	(`spawn_order`).
162	
163	- Where the configuration can run computations side by side, `spawn`
164	  returns at once (`side_by_side: true`).
165	- Where it cannot, the first runs to its end or its budget, and then the
166	  next (`side_by_side: false`).
167	- Each spawned computation has its own budget and its own execution
168	  state, recorded separately.
169	- P16b only: where the configuration does not allow separate
170	  computations to share unknowns, the four contributions are posed as one
171	  conjunction in `main` (`spawn_fallback`), with `fallback_queries`, and
172	  that is recorded. Which configurations allow it is the systems file's
173	  and the system harness's statement, not the harness's judgement on a
174	  run.
175	
176	The harness may use the configuration's own mechanism for starting a
177	computation (an engine, a thread, a program's own spawn), as the program
178	asks for it. It may not interleave computations itself.
179	
180	### answers(cap)
181	
182	Collects the answers the system reports, **through its standard mechanism
183	for enumerating them** (each systems file says what it is; for Python and
184	ALGOL 60 it is the values the program prints), until the mechanism is
185	exhausted, the budget runs out, or `cap` answers have been collected.
186	`cap` is 1 for an *any one* query and 20 otherwise, as `stages.json`
187	gives it per query. The harness never asks for an answer the mechanism
188	did not offer, never filters or deduplicates answers, and never stops
189	early because the answers look complete. Each answer is recorded
190	**verbatim**, as the mechanism produced it, with `ended_by`:
191	
192	| ended_by | when |
193	|---|---|
194	| `exhausted` | the mechanism reported no more answers |
195	| `cap` | `cap` answers were collected; the mechanism was not asked again |
196	| `budget` | the budget ran out while collecting |
197	| `timeout` | the safety limit stopped the attempt |
198	| `error` | the system stopped with an error |
199	| `no-enumeration` | the configuration has no mechanism for asking for more: the program printed what it computed for the stage and the stage ended (Python, ALGOL 60) |
200	
201	The execution state is classified **after** the call (section 5).
202	
203	### observe()
204	
205	Records the state the common observations need (`SPECIFICATION.md`,
206	"Observations common to every problem"), **verbatim**, as the system or
207	the program holds it at the end of the stage, including at the moment a
208	budget runs out: bindings held (`SPECIFICATION.md`, "reported": a binding
209	is reported if `observe()` can read it), residual relations, suspended
210	work, alternatives held. `observe.raw` is what was read, unedited;
211	`observe.bindings` splits it by unknown only where that can be done
212	mechanically. A residual counts as reported only if it is state that the
213	system or program holds and acts on later; printing the posed information
214	back is not observing it, and the harness never makes a residual up from
215	the posed information.
216	
217	### print()
218	
219	The system's own rendering of what it holds at the end of the stage (an
220	Absys assertion's printed derivations, a Prolog toplevel's bindings, the
221	program's printed values), recorded verbatim in `print`. The harness
222	never reformats it.
223	
224	### Observing must not consume the computation
225	
226	In a configuration where collecting answers or observing would end or
227	alter the computation that the next stage extends (exhausting a
228	backtracking search in a SWI-Prolog *session* engine, for instance),
229	`answers()` and `observe()` for stage k are taken on a **separate run of
230	stages 1 to k**, and the incremental computation is left as it was. The
231	record marks each such query `collected_on: "separate-run"`, and the
232	observation `taken_on: "separate-run"`, and keeps the separate run's
233	stdout, stderr and steps under `separate_run`. Its P11 effects go to the
234	observation log (section 6). In a reposed configuration every stage's run
235	is already separate, and nothing more is needed.
236	
237	## 5. Execution state
238	
239	Recorded per computation, per attempt, in the vocabulary of
240	`SPECIFICATION.md` ("Execution state"), **as far as the harness can tell
241	it mechanically**:
242	
243	| state | what the harness reads to say so |
244	|---|---|
245	| `budget` | its budget mechanism fired (Absys `--steps`, `call_with_inference_limit/3`, the `sys.monitoring` callback, `--max-steps`) |
246	| `timeout` | the safety limit stopped the attempt |
247	| `error` | the system stopped with an error; the error is copied verbatim to `error_verbatim` |
248	| `alternatives pending` | the system's own report that a request for more answers would resume it (a nondeterministic exit, open choicepoints, hibernating derivations), or, for Python and ALGOL 60, the program's named pending structure, read by `observe()` |
249	| `suspended` | the system's own report of held work that later information may resume (suspended equations, attributed variables with goals, a blocked engine, a program's named queue) |
250	| `finished` | the system stopped and reports none of the above |
251	
252	`alternatives pending` and `suspended` may both hold. `finished` excludes
253	the others; at most one of `budget`, `timeout` and `error` holds. Where
254	the harness cannot tell mechanically, it says so (`determined: false`),
255	lists what it could tell, and gives its basis. **The harness never
256	classifies the semantic axis, the representation, the simplification or
257	the effects class**: those are the classifiers' (`PROTOCOL.md`, "Roles"),
258	from the record.
259	
260	## 6. Commitments and the effects log (P11)
261	
262	**Commitments are preserved when a run is reposed.** At a commit stage
263	(`stages.json`, `commit: true`: P11c stage 3, P11d stage 2), the system
264	selects one of its current outcomes, v, and reports it through its
265	answers mechanism (`answers(1)`). The harness keeps that answer verbatim.
266	When a later stage is reposed, the commit stage is replayed **as the
267	information x = v**, with v passed to the program verbatim as first
268	selected, and recorded in `posed.replayed_commitments`. The harness never
269	asks the system to select again, and never parses or rewrites v beyond
270	taking the answer as the system gave it. Where the system did not select
271	(one that keeps every alternative live), nothing is replayed as a
272	commitment, and that is recorded; the classifiers judge it as P11 says.
273	In P11a and P11b, which have one stage, the outcome is committed when it
274	is reported (`committed_when_reported`).
275	
276	**The effects log.** The harness provides L and emit: one stub, with the
277	same behaviour and the same log format in every system (the binding of
278	emit into each language is the system harness's).
279	
280	- `emit(m)` appends one entry, m as the program passed it, rendered as
281	  the system renders m, to the log, and returns. It does nothing else: it
282	  does not fail, defer, buffer past the end of the stage, deduplicate, or
283	  read the log. Nothing the system does can remove an entry.
284	- The log is a file of JSON lines, one entry per line, with the fields of
285	  `effect_entry` in the schema: `seq` (position, from 1, never reused),
286	  `entry`, `run_id`, `stage`, `attempt`, `during_replay_of` (the earlier
287	  stage being replayed when emit was called, in a reposed run, else
288	  null), and `log`.
289	- **One classification log per configuration and instance**, at
290	  `results/<system>/<configuration>/P11/raw/<instance>.effects.jsonl`,
291	  **never reset**, across every behaviour run the harness makes, reposed
292	  runs and safety reruns included. The record copies the entries this run
293	  appended into each attempt's `effects`, and the whole log after the run
294	  into `effects.log_after_run`, with `entries_before_run`.
295	- **Separate observation runs** (section 4) and **every cost and storage
296	  run** write to `<instance>.effects-observation.jsonl` in the same
297	  folder, which is not judged (Q8).
298	- Entries emitted while replaying an earlier stage carry
299	  `during_replay_of`, so that entries duplicated only by reposing can be
300	  counted separately. The harness marks when an entry was made; whether it
301	  is a duplicate, and whether it was before, at or after commitment, is
302	  for the classifiers.
303	
304	## 7. Budget and safety limit
305	
306	| | P12, P13, P16 | every other problem |
307	|---|---|---|
308	| budget | 10⁸ steps per stage and computation | 10⁶ steps per stage and computation |
309	| safety limit | 600 s per stage, **fixed, no rerun** | 60 s per stage, then **one rerun at 600 s** |
310	| source | the problem file (`stages.json`, `limits`) | `PROTOCOL.md`, "Running" |
311	
312	- **Steps** are in the systems file's unit (Absys steps, SWI-Prolog
313	  inferences, Python bytecode instructions, ALGOL 60 interpreter ticks).
314	  The budget is a classification within a system, never compared across
315	  systems. Each spawned computation has its own budget; P16b stages 2
316	  and 3 have one for the whole.
317	- **A reposed run** has a budget of its **measured restart cost plus
318	  10⁶** (10⁸ where the problem says). The restart cost is always
319	  measured, in the system's step unit, never estimated or taken from
320	  another run (Q6):
321	  - **in-run** (the default): the harness reads the system's step count
322	    at the moment stage k is first posed in the reposed run, after the
323	    replay of stages 1 to k−1. That count is the restart cost, and the
324	    stage then has 10⁶ more steps: its budget is the restart cost plus
325	    10⁶. During the replay each replayed stage has the budget it had
326	    when first posed (10⁶ each);
327	  - **separate-run**, only where the system cannot read its count at that
328	    moment: the harness first runs stages 1 to k−1 alone, posed exactly
329	    as in the replay and with no `answers()` call, and measures its
330	    steps; that is the restart cost, and the reposed run's budget is it
331	    plus 10⁶.
332	
333	  It is recorded in `steps.restart_cost`, with `restart_cost_method`
334	  (`in-run` or `separate-run`) and `restart_cost_source`. The only
335	  exception is a configuration with no step count at all (ALGOL 60
336	  x1sim, Q12), whose records have `budget_enforced: false` and
337	  `restart_cost: null`.
338	- **After budget.** If stage k ends in *budget* and the configuration can
339	  keep its computation and continue it, stage k+1 is posed into that same
340	  computation, with a new budget (`continued_after_budget: true`). Only
341	  where it cannot are stages 1 to k+1 reposed (`reason: "after-budget"`),
342	  counted under restart cost. Whether a configuration can continue is the
343	  system harness's statement, in its README.
344	- **After error.** Stage k+1 is posed by reposing stages 1 to k+1
345	  (`reason: "after-error"`), counted under restart cost, in every
346	  configuration, incremental ones included.
347	- **After timeout.** As after error: the stopped computation cannot be
348	  continued, so stage k+1 is reposed (`reason: "after-timeout"`), Q7.
349	- **Safety limit.** It protects the harness; it is not a measurement.
350	  It covers one attempt of one stage: for an incremental stage, from
351	  posing stage k to the end of `print()`; for a reposed stage, the whole
352	  run of stages 1 to k. When it stops an attempt, the harness stops the
353	  system by the means its README gives (`safety_limit.how_stopped`),
354	  records the attempt with what it had collected, and, where the problem
355	  allows, **reruns the stage once** with the limit raised tenfold
356	  (attempt 2, `reason: "safety-rerun"`). An incremental configuration's
357	  rerun is reposed, since the stopped computation is gone. If the rerun
358	  also stops, *timeout* is final for that stage (`final-timeout`). Under
359	  a fixed limit (P12, P13, P16) the first stop is final
360	  (`fixed-limit-timeout`). **Both attempts are recorded.** Answers
361	  collected before a stop are kept and classified on the semantic axis;
362	  only the execution state is *timeout*.
363	- A run that hits the safety limit only because it is instrumented (cost
364	  or storage, where the behaviour run finished) is recorded as such; it
365	  is not evidence about the model (`PROTOCOL.md`, "Modes of running").
366	  The classifiers read that from the records of the two modes.
367	- **ALGOL 60 x1sim** has no step count, so no budget can be enforced;
368	  only the safety limit stops it, and its records say
369	  `budget_enforced: false` (Q12).
370	
371	## 8. Modes
372	
373	Each program is run in up to three modes, one run each. A run's record
374	says its mode, and each figure is taken from the mode that gives it:
375	
376	| mode | instrumentation | gives |
377	|---|---|---|
378	| **behaviour** | none beyond the harness (its budget counter included) | answers, observe(), print(), the execution state, the effects log. **The semantic result and the execution state are taken from this run** |
379	| **cost** | step counting only | steps per stage (incremental and restated), restart cost, answer latency (steps to the first answer, between answers, to the end), problem operations, repeated work where the systems file names a source, candidates examined (P12) |
380	| **storage** | the systems file's storage measurement | store vector (boundary and peak), retained alternatives (at answers, at boundaries, at budget, peak), suspended state (at boundaries and peak), P13's maximum resident set size where the systems file takes it from a separate run |
381	
382	- **A sampled measurement is never taken from the run that gives the step
383	  count or the classification.** A sampled maximum (`peak.kind =
384	  "sampled"`) may appear only in a storage record; `validate.py` rejects
385	  one in a behaviour or cost record. Exact peaks may appear in any mode
386	  whose instrumentation gives them.
387	- A field a mode does not measure is `null`, or `{}` for the store
388	  vector. Figures that a mode records incidentally (the budget counter's
389	  steps in a behaviour run) are kept, but the figure of record is the one
390	  from the mode in this table.
391	- Where two modes can be compared, their answers must agree; a
392	  disagreement is reported as a fault of the instrumentation, by the
393	  classifiers, from the records.
394	- The systems file says which modes a configuration has (x1sim:
395	  behaviour only). P13's process CPU time and maximum resident set size
396	  are recorded where the systems file says, for growth only.
397	
398	## 9. The raw record
399	
400	One JSON file per run, valid against [`record.schema.json`](record.schema.json),
401	the same for every system. Every string the system produced is kept
402	**verbatim** (JSON-escaped, never trimmed, reflowed or decoded beyond the
403	system's own output encoding; bytes that are not UTF-8 are written as
404	`�` and noted in `harness_faults`). A value the harness could not
405	read is `null`, never estimated.
406	
407	### Run metadata (`run`)
408	
409	| field | what |
410	|---|---|
411	| `run_id` | unique, also the file's stem: `<instance>.<mode>.<UTC timestamp YYYYMMDDTHHMMSSZ>` |
412	| `spec_tag` | `spec-1.0` |
413	| `system`, `configuration` | as in `systems/` |
414	| `problem`, `subproblem`, `instance`, `parameters` | from `stages.json`; `parameters` copied exactly |
415	| `mode` | behaviour, cost or storage |
416	| `purpose` | `primary`, `variant` (the verifier's), `qualification`, `example` (made up) |
417	| `program` | `path` and `sha256` of the program file as run, and the repository commit it was taken from |
418	| `constants` | `block`, `input` or `none`; the input file's path and SHA-256; the hidden variant's id when the verifier runs one |
419	| `system_build` | the pinned `commit` (from `/opt/src/COMMITS` in `cp-systems`), the `image` digest, the `binary`, the system's `version_output` verbatim, and whether the build or run is `instrumented` |
420	| `harness` | the harness's path, its git commit, and whether its files differed from it (`dirty`) |
421	| `command` | the harness command line as invoked |
422	| `posing` | `incremental` or `reposed`: the configuration's way of receiving a stage |
423	| `limits` | `budget_steps`, `step_unit`, `safety_limit_s`, `rerun_limit_s` |
424	| `started_utc`, `ended_utc`, `complete`, `incomplete_reason` | |
425	| `confounds`, `environment` | the system harness's listed confounds; environment it set (`PYTHONHASHSEED=0`, for instance) |
426	
427	### Per stage, per attempt (`stages[].attempts[]`)
428	
429	| field | what |
430	|---|---|
431	| `attempt`, `limit_s` | 1 under 60 s (600 s for P12, P13, P16); 2 for the rerun under 600 s |
432	| `posed` | `how` (`fresh`, `incremental`, `reposed`), `reason` (`first-stage`, `configuration`, `after-budget`, `after-error`, `after-timeout`, `safety-rerun`), `replayed` (the earlier stages replayed, `[1 … k−1]` when reposed), `replayed_commitments` (P11), `continued_after_budget`, `instance_parameters_passed` |
433	| `computations[]` | per computation: `id`, `spawned`, `spawn_index`, `side_by_side`; its `queries` (each with `id`, `cap`, `answers` verbatim with `steps_at` and `alternatives_at` where measured, `ended_by`, `collected_on`); its `execution_state` (`states`, `determined`, `basis`, `error_verbatim`); its `steps` (`unit`, `budget`, `budget_exhausted`, `budget_enforced`, incremental `stage`, `restated`, `restart_cost` with `restart_cost_method`, `to_first_answer`, `between_answers`, `to_end`, `repeated_work`); its `alternatives` in the systems file's unit (`at_boundary`, `at_budget`, `peak`, `held_as`: all live at once or kept for backtracking, `by_type`, `problem_defined`); its `suspended` work in the system's own terms (`at_boundary`, `peak`, `items` by kind with counts); `problem_operations` by relation case; `candidates_examined` (P12) |
434	| `observe` | `raw` verbatim, `method`, `taken_on`, `bindings` |
435	| `print` | verbatim |
436	| `store` | the systems file's vector, by quantity: `boundary`, `peak` (`exact` or `sampled`, with its interval) |
437	| `wall_time_s`, `cpu_time_s`, `max_rss_kb` | wall time (for the safety limit, not a metric); CPU and RSS for P13 growth only |
438	| `stdout`, `stderr` | verbatim, everything the system and program wrote during the attempt |
439	| `exit` | status and signal, or null where the process continues into the next stage |
440	| `safety_limit` | `hit`, `action` (`none`, `rerun`, `final-timeout`, `fixed-limit-timeout`), `how_stopped` |
441	| `effects` | P11: the log entries this attempt appended |
442	| `manual_actions` | every action by a person, or by code written for one problem, that the fixed harness does not perform (`METRICS.md`, "Intervention"), with who and why |
443	| `separate_run` | the separate run of stages 1 to k, where answers or observation were taken on one |
444	
445	At record level: `effects` (P11: the logs' paths and the whole
446	classification log after the run; null otherwise), `manual_actions`
447	outside any stage, `harness_faults` (what the harness itself failed to
448	do), `notes`.
449	
450	### Rules a record must keep (checked by `validate.py`)
451	
452	Beyond the schema:
453	
454	1. The instance exists in `stages.json`, with the same problem,
455	   sub-problem and parameters, and the problem's limits; a complete run
456	   has every stage, numbered 1 … K.
457	2. Each stage's queries are those of `stages.json`, on the computations it
458	   names, with its caps; spawned computations are those it spawns, in the
459	   instance's `spawn_order` (or the P16b fallback).
460	3. No query has more answers than its cap; `ended_by: "cap"` has exactly
461	   cap answers; `ended_by` budget, timeout or error appears in the
462	   computation's state.
463	4. Stage 1 is `fresh`. A reposed stage replays exactly 1 … k−1. An
464	   incremental stage replays nothing, and is not used in a reposing
465	   configuration except to continue after budget. After an error the next
466	   stage is reposed. A `continued_after_budget` stage follows a *budget*.
467	5. A reposed stage has a measured restart cost, with its method, and
468	   its budget is that plus the problem's budget; any other stage's is the
469	   problem's budget. Only a computation with `budget_enforced: false`
470	   may have no restart cost.
471	6. A second attempt exists only after the safety limit stopped the first,
472	   under the problem's rerun limit; none under a fixed limit. A *timeout*
473	   state and a safety-limit stop go together.
474	7. `finished` stands alone; at most one of budget, timeout, error;
475	   *error* has its text; *budget* matches `budget_exhausted`.
476	8. No sampled maximum outside a storage record.
477	9. A separate run, where one is used, replays 1 … k.
478	10. P11 records have `effects`; others do not. The entries of the
479	    attempts are exactly the classification log's entries after
480	    `entries_before_run`; cost and storage runs write only to the
481	    observation log; replayed commitments are for earlier commit stages.
482	
483	```
484	python3 harnesses/validate.py results/<system>/<configuration>/<problem>/raw/*.json
485	python3 harnesses/validate.py --check-stages            # checks stages.json itself
486	python3 harnesses/validate.py --stages harnesses/examples/stages-made-up.json harnesses/examples/made-up-*.json
487	```
488	
489	The last line runs on the made-up examples: three valid records (an
490	incremental run with a safety-limit rerun; a reposing run with a commit
491	and the effects log; two spawned computations in a storage run with a
492	separate observation run) and one deliberately invalid record, which it
493	rejects with six errors.
494	
495	## 10. Where records go
496	
497	    results/<system>/<configuration>/<problem>/raw/<run_id>.json
498	    results/<system>/<configuration>/P11/raw/<instance>.effects.jsonl
499	    results/<system>/<configuration>/P11/raw/<instance>.effects-observation.jsonl
500	
501	`OUTDIR` is that `raw/` folder. A harness never overwrites or deletes a
502	record: every run, including reruns, failed runs and runs on hidden
503	variants (`purpose: "variant"`, written under the verifier's own
504	`OUTDIR`), is kept. The result files of `PROTOCOL.md`, "Recording a
505	result" (`results/<system>/<configuration>/<problem>.md`) are written
506	from these records by the classifiers, and cite them by `run_id`.
507	
508	## 11. What a program must provide
509	
510	A program author cannot run anything before the program is fixed (only
511	the system harness's `check`, which executes nothing). So each system
512	harness's README says exactly, per configuration, how a program meets
513	these requirements; the common part is:
514	
515	1. **Stages as units the harness can pose.** The program handles stage k
516	   when, and only when, the harness poses it, in the way the
517	   configuration receives stages (incremental, or by replaying 1 … k).
518	   Code for stage k does not depend on any later stage.
519	2. **Replay.** In a reposed run the program carries out every stage
520	   1 … k in order, replacements and withdrawals included, and accepts a
521	   replayed commit stage as the information x = v, with v as the harness
522	   passes it (the verbatim answer of the commit stage).
523	3. **Instance parameters.** The program takes n, an arrival order, a
524	   spawn order or the answer mode from the harness, as `stages.json`
525	   names them, and holds everything else.
526	4. **Answers through the standard mechanism.** Answers reach the harness
527	   only through the configuration's standard mechanism for answers, in
528	   the form the system harness's README fixes (for Python and ALGOL 60,
529	   printed lines with the delimiters it defines).
530	5. **State for observe().** Whatever the system does not expose by
531	   itself (a Python program's named pending structure, its counters of
532	   problem operations), the program exposes in the form the system
533	   harness reads. Counters that only count are H (`METRICS.md`).
534	6. **Constants for the verifier** (`PROTOCOL.md`, "Writing a program",
535	   rule 6). Every constant of every stage is in **one** place the
536	   verifier can replace without touching anything else, and the program
537	   stays correct for other constants. Which place is fixed per system by
538	   its harness README, not here, with this default:
539	
540	   | system | where the constants are |
541	   |---|---|
542	   | ALGOL 60 | **input**: read with the input procedures as integers in the problem's encoding (`systems/algol-60/README.md`, "Values"), from a constants file the harness passes; recorded as `constants.how = "input"` with its SHA-256 |
543	   | Absys, SWI-Prolog, Python | **one marked constants block** in the program, between a line containing `CONSTANTS BEGIN` and a line containing `CONSTANTS END`, each inside a comment of the language, holding nothing but the constants, or **input**, as the system harness decides and documents; recorded as `block` or `input` |
544	
545	   A sub-problem with no constants (P04d, P04f, P08b; `variants/README.md`)
546	   records `none`. Sizes n and arrival orders are not constants (they are
547	   not varied) and come from the harness (point 3).
548	7. **Provenance** (`PROTOCOL.md`, "Writing a program", rules 1, 2, 8): its
549	   author, whether the author had seen a precursor, and the source of each
550	   idiom, in a comment the system harness README places.
551	
552	**H tokens** (`METRICS.md`, class H) are the per-system harness's own
553	calls as they appear in a program: the calls that pose stages, request
554	answers and print, the emit stub's binding, and output adapters (rule
555	13). Each system harness's README lists them, construct by construct,
556	before any program is written. Code a program adds beyond them is
557	classed by the rules of `METRICS.md`, not as H.
558	
559	## 12. What every system harness writes
560	
561	As its brief says (`sandbox/briefs/harness-system.md`), under
562	`harnesses/<system>/`: `run` with this command line for every
563	configuration and every mode the systems file allows, for every problem
564	P01–P16, spawn and the effects log included; `check CONFIGURATION
565	PROGRAM`, which executes nothing; a `README.md` with the program contract
566	of section 11 for its system, a complete minimal example for a made-up
567	problem, the H tokens, how it stops a system at the safety limit, whether
568	each configuration can continue after budget, and its confounds;
569	`S-mechanisms.md`; and `qualification/`, whose every record passes
570	`validate.py`. Anything it cannot do as this file says goes in its own
571	`QUESTIONS.md`, with the reading it implemented.
572	<class 'dict'>
573	['format', 'spec_tag', 'about', 'vocabulary', 'default_limits', 'problems']

37	## 1. Configurations, posing and modes
38	
39	From `systems/swi-prolog/README.md`:
40	
41	| configuration | adds to plain | posing (`run.posing`) | a new computation is |
42	|---|---|---|---|
43	| `plain` | nothing | reposed | a fresh `swipl` process per stage attempt |
44	| `tabling` | `:- table` | reposed | the same |
45	| `coroutines` | `when/2`, `freeze/2`, `dif/2` | reposed | the same |
46	| `constraints` | coroutines, `library(clpfd)`, `library(clpq)` | reposed | the same |
47	| `session` | constraints, engines, and S code that waits for an undefined procedure | incremental | one engine in one `swipl` process holds the computation; each stage is posted into it |
48	
49	Every configuration has all three modes (`behaviour`, `cost`, `storage`;
50	the systems file restricts none). A fresh process per stage gives every
51	reposed run the same load sequence, autoload state and empty database
52	(`measurement.md`, "Fixed run conditions"), and makes the reposed run a
53	new computation: anything a program asserted is gone.
54	
55	`swipl` is always started as `swipl -f none --no-tty -q -g
56	cp_harness:h_main(CTL) -t halt(4) harnesses/swi-prolog/lib/harness.pl`:
57	no init file, not in debug mode, `optimise` false (the default), `gc`
58	true, the default 1 GB stack limit, `occurs_check` false and `unknown`
59	error (SWI's and ISO's defaults; a program that is the systems file's
60	recorded variant sets them itself by a directive, which the record shows
61	in the `loaded` flags). Standard input is `/dev/null`.

63	## 2. The program contract
64	
65	A program for SWI-Prolog is **one Prolog source file**, loaded into module
66	`user` with `load_files/2` (so: no `:- module` declaration), **without its
67	CONSTANTS block**: the driver blanks the block's lines (so line numbers
68	stay the same) and loads that copy; the block never reaches the system as
69	program text (§ 2.5). It may load
70	libraries with `:- use_module(library(...))` directives, and must for
71	operators such as clpfd's. After loading, the harness calls
72	`autoload_all/0` (and restores the `autoload` flag it switches off), so
73	that no library is autoloaded while a stage is measured. Directives run
74	when the file is loaded, before any stage; they must not pose stages or
75	print answers. A program must not read standard input, define a module,
76	or define any of the H predicates below or `'$cp_query'/1`.
77	
78	### 2.1 What the program defines
79	
80	| predicate | meaning | class |
81	|---|---|---|
82	| `unknowns(Computation, Names)` | for each computation (`main`, or a spawned computation's id as `stages.json` names it, e.g. `'A'`), the names of its unknowns, a list of atoms that are Prolog variable names (`['X', 'Y']`). Use the sub-problem's unknowns from `stages.json`, capitalised, or names that hold several of them (`'Xs'`). The harness makes one fresh variable per name, and the answers are rendered with these names. | H |
83	| `stage(K, Vars, Constants)` | the information of stage K, as a goal over `Vars`, the list of `main`'s unknowns in the order of `Names`. `Constants` is the list of the CONSTANTS block's entries for stages 1 … K, in the block's order (§ 2.5): the only way a constant reaches the program. One clause (or several) per stage number. Stage K's code may not depend on any later stage (rule 5), and cannot see a later stage's constants. | head H; body P/C/R/S by `METRICS.md` |
84	| `query(K, Vars)` | the query posed after stage K, over the same `Vars`: usually `query(_, _).` (the stages' goals bind the unknowns themselves); for a problem whose stages replace or withdraw named quantities held in the database (`assertz/1`, `retract/1`), the goal that reads them (`query(_, [V]) :- v(V).`). Must be defined. | head H; body classed |
85	| `spawned(K, Computation, Vars, Constants)` | only where stage K spawns computations (P09a, P09b): the goal of that computation, over its own unknowns, with stage K's constants as for `stage/3` | head H; body classed |
86	
87	The harness numbers stages 1 … K as `stages.json` does (P16d2's two stages
88	are 1 and 2). It never passes a constant: the program holds every stage's
89	information.
90	
91	### 2.2 How a stage is posed
92	
93	**plain, tabling, coroutines, constraints (reposed).** For stage k the
94	harness starts a fresh process, loads the program, and compiles one clause
95	
96	    '$cp_query'(Bindings) :- h_m(1), stage(1, Vars, C1), h_m(2), stage(2, Vars, C2), …, h_m(k), stage(k, Vars, Ck), query(k, Vars).
97	
98	where Cj is the list of the block's entries for stages 1 … j.
99	
100	and runs it as a query. Stages 1 … k−1 are thereby replayed **in order,
101	every one of them**, replacements and withdrawals included: the program
102	carries them out (`PROTOCOL.md`, pose). `h_m(J)` is the harness's stage
103	mark: on the first entry into stage J's part it records the step count
104	(for stage k: the in-run restart cost) and gives stage J its budget (§ 9);
105	on every entry it records which stage's code is running (for `emit/1`).
106	Its inferences are excluded from the steps.
107	
108	**session (incremental).** One process; the harness creates one engine
109	whose goal is the harness's loop, and for each stage posts the message
110	`stage(J, …)` with `engine_post/3`. Inside the engine the posted stages
111	form one growing conjunction, `stage(1, Vars, C1), …, stage(L, Vars, CL)`, L
112	the latest stage posted: the engine marks and calls `stage(J, Vars, CJ)`, and when
113	the computation reaches the end of stage L it yields to the harness and
114	waits for the next message. If the computation later backtracks into an
115	earlier stage and comes forward again, the stages after it that were
116	already posted are called again from the harness's record, without a new
117	message, as in any conjunction. `query(K, Vars)` is called only where the
118	answers are collected (§ 3). A stage after a stage that ended in budget,
119	error or timeout, or after the engine's computation failed (no solution
120	left, so nothing can receive the next stage; `QUESTIONS.md`, S3), starts a
121	new engine in a new process, into which stages 1 … k−1 are posted again
122	(`posed.how = reposed`, replayed), and then k, k+1, … incrementally.
123	
124	In *session* the configuration's supporting code (`S/session-wait.pl`)
125	is loaded before the program: a call of a procedure that has no
126	definition waits, in the engine, until a later stage defines it (as
127	`h_wait/0` does), instead of raising the existence error.
128	
129	**Spawned computations** (P09a, P09b): `spawned(1, C, Vars, C1)` for each
130	computation C in the instance's `spawn_order`, each as a separate query in
131	the same process (sharing its database), with its own budget, run to its
132	end or its budget before the next (`side_by_side: false`), in every
133	configuration. **P16b**: no SWI-Prolog configuration lets separate
134	computations share unknowns (a separate query, or an engine, copies its
135	goal), so P16b's stage 1 is always posed as one conjunction in `main`
136	(`spawn_fallback`): the program's `stage(1, Vars, C1)` is the conjunction of
137	the four contributions.
138	
139	### 2.3 The H predicates a program may call
140	
141	All are exported by the harness into `user`. Their inferences, call
142	port included, are excluded from the steps and the budget (§ 9), so a
143	program's steps are the same with and without them (qualification, "H
144	calls").
145	
146	| call | what it does |
147	|---|---|
148	| `h_param(Name, Value)` | the instance's parameters, as `stages.json` gives them: `n`, `order` (a list of atoms, e.g. `['R2','R1','R3']`, `['312']`… as written there), `answers` (`all`, `'any-one'`), `cap`, `spawn_order`. Fails for a name the instance does not have |
149	| `h_commitment(V)` | in the code of a commit stage (P11c stage 3, P11d stage 2): succeeds, with V the string the commit stage first reported (the verbatim answer, e.g. `"X = 1 "`), when that stage is being replayed in a reposed run with a selected value; fails otherwise (when the stage is first posed, or nothing was selected). The program turns V into its information x = v itself (for instance `term_string(T, V, [variable_names(Bs)])`) |
150	| `emit(M)` | P11's effects stub: appends one entry to the effects log, M rendered with `answer_write_options` (`~W`), and returns. It does nothing else, never fails |
151	| `h_count(Name)` | one application of a case of a relation the problem defines, counted under `Name` (`'conc/1'`): `problem_operations` |
152	| `h_candidate` | P12: one sequence for which accept(s) is evaluated: `candidates_examined` |
153	| `h_held(Name, Count)` | problem-defined alternatives held now (P05's values of x, P12's partial sequences, P15a's interleavings); the last value at the stage's end is recorded in `alternatives.problem_defined` |
154	| `h_wait` | session only: the computation waits here for the next stage. The harness records the stage as ended with the computation waiting (*suspended*); when it posts the next stage, `h_wait` receives it into this computation (marks it and calls its `stage/3`) and returns. Outside session it raises a permission error |

156	### 2.4 Answers
157	
158	Answers are the solutions of the posed query, collected by backtracking,
159	the system's standard mechanism: the harness asks for the next solution
160	only while the previous one left choicepoints and fewer than `cap`
161	answers have been collected, exactly as the toplevel offers `;` only for a
162	nondeterministic answer. Each answer is recorded **as the toplevel renders
163	it**: the harness calls the toplevel's own `'$toplevel':translate_bindings/4`
164	and `name_vars/3` and formats the `query(yes(…))` message (an answer
165	without choicepoints, ending `.`) or the `query(more(…))` message (one
166	with), with the toplevel's `answer_write_options` except `max_depth(0)`
167	for `max_depth(10)`, so that nothing is elided. Residual goals (freeze,
168	dif, clpfd, …) appear as the toplevel shows them; cyclic terms in the
169	toplevel's `% where` form. The rendering happens under `\+ \+`, so it binds
170	nothing. For a made-up stage the qualification checks the texts against
171	the real toplevel's output byte for byte.
172	
173	A program reports answers only through its unknowns: anything it prints
174	is recorded in the stage's `stdout`, verbatim, but is not an answer.
175	
176	`ended_by`: `exhausted` when the last request failed, or the last answer
177	had no choicepoint; `cap`; `budget`; `error`; `timeout`. In session, at a
178	stage that is not the instance's last, answers are collected on a
179	**separate run** of stages 1 … k (a fresh process and engine, stages 1 …
180	k−1 posted as replay, then k with its query; `collected_on:
181	separate-run`), because backtracking for further answers would consume
182	the incremental computation that the next stage extends (common contract,
183	section 4). At the instance's last stage nothing extends the computation,
184	and its answers are collected in it. A separate run's effects go to the
185	observation log.
186	
187	### 2.5 Constants
188	
189	Every constant of every stage is in **one marked block** of the file,
190	between a comment line containing `CONSTANTS BEGIN` and a comment line
191	containing `CONSTANTS END`. Inside it each entry is a Prolog fact, and
192	each entry is **tagged with the stage that first uses it**: a comment line
193	`% stage K` starts the entries of stage K, the stages in increasing order,
194	and nothing but comments and blank lines comes before the first. A stage
195	that adds no constant has no section. For example:
196	
197	    % CONSTANTS BEGIN
198	    % stage 1
199	    colour(red).
200	    colour(green).
201	    % stage 3
202	    first_colour(green).
203	    % CONSTANTS END
204	
205	The verifier replaces the block and nothing else; the program must stay
206	correct for other constants (rule 6).
207	
208	**No anticipation, made structural** (rule 5). The block is never loaded
209	as program text: the driver reads the file, splits the block by its
210	`% stage K` lines, and loads the program with the block's lines blanked.
211	A stage's entries reach the system only when that stage is posed: in a
212	reposed configuration, the process that poses stage k is given the
213	entries of stages 1 … k and no others (stage 1's process holds nothing of
214	stage 2's, as text or as terms); in *session*, stage k's entries are sent
215	with the command that posts stage k, and only then read. They reach the
216	program only as the last argument of `stage(J, Vars, Constants)` (and of
217	`spawned/4`): the list of the entries of stages 1 … J, read as terms when
218	stage J's goal is built or posted, and again on every replay. A program
219	that needs them as clauses asserts them itself in the stage that brings
220	them (`forall(member(E, Cs), assertz(E))`, with a `dynamic` declaration);
221	that is the program's code. The qualification checks that at stages 1
222	and 2 nothing of stage 3's constant is among the process's atoms or
223	strings, and that at stage 3 it is (`programs/xlate.pl`).
224	
225	`run` records `constants.how = block` when it finds one such block, and
226	`none` when it finds none (a sub-problem without constants: P04d, P04f,
227	P08b). A malformed block (two pairs, entries before any `% stage K`,
228	stages not increasing) is a usage error (exit 2), and `check` reports it.
229	Sizes and orders are not constants: they come from `h_param/2`.
230

243	### 2.7 A complete minimal example
244	
245	A made-up problem X01, not one of P01–P16 (`qualification/stages-made-up.json`):
246	two unknowns a and b, the stripes of a flag; stage 1, a is a colour;
247	stage 2, b is a colour other than a's; stage 3, a is the given first
248	colour. All answers (cap 20).
249	
250	```prolog
251	% Made-up problem X01 (not one of P01-P16): the two stripes of a flag.
252	% Stage 1: stripe a is a colour. Stage 2: stripe b is a colour other than
253	% a's. Stage 3: a is the given first colour.
254	%
255	% PROVENANCE
256	%   author: harness-swi-prolog (the harness author), for the qualification
257	%   precursor seen: none (a made-up problem)
258	%   idioms: conjunctive queries, ISO Prolog; member/2 and memberchk/2 of
259	%   library(lists) over the stage's constants
260	% END PROVENANCE
261	
262	% CONSTANTS BEGIN
263	% stage 1
264	colour(red).
265	colour(green).
266	colour(blue).
267	% stage 3
268	first_colour(green).
269	% CONSTANTS END
270	
271	unknowns(main, ['A', 'B']).
272	
273	stage(1, [A, _], Cs) :- member(colour(A), Cs).
274	stage(2, [A, B], Cs) :- member(colour(B), Cs), B \== A.
275	stage(3, [A, _], Cs) :- memberchk(first_colour(A), Cs).
276	
277	query(_, _).
278	```
279	
280	Stage 1 receives `[colour(red), colour(green), colour(blue)]`, stage 2 the
281	same, stage 3 that and `first_colour(green)`; the processes that pose
282	stages 1 and 2 never see `first_colour(green)`. In *plain*, stage 3 is
283	posed as `stage(1, V, C1), stage(2, V, C2), stage(3, V, C3), query(3, V)`
284	in a fresh process; its answers are recorded as `"A = green,\nB = red "`
285	and `"A = green,\nB = blue "`, `ended_by: exhausted`, state *finished*.
286	The same file runs in every configuration; in *session* stages 1 and 2
287	take their answers from separate runs and stage 3 from the engine itself.
288	[`qualification/programs/`](qualification/programs) holds the other
289	made-up programs, among them `x02-commit.pl` (emit/1 and h_commitment/1),
290	`x03-spawn.pl` (spawned/4), `x09-count.pl` (h_param/2, h_count/1,
291	h_held/2), `x11-replace.pl` (a replacing stage, with query/2) and
292	`x08-wait.pl` (h_wait/0).

294	## 3. observe() and print()
295	
296	**observe()** reads, at the end of the stage, the state the computation
297	holds, verbatim (`observe.raw`):
298	
299	- where the computation is still at an answer (the last answer had
300	  choicepoints and the cap stopped collection, or it had none): the
301	  toplevel's rendering of the bindings and residual goals held there;
302	- in session, at a stage whose answers come from a separate run: the
303	  incremental computation's own state at the end of the stage, read in the
304	  engine without consuming it (`taken_on: this-run`);
305	- at the moment the budget runs out, or an error reaches the harness,
306	  before the stacks unwind: the same rendering, read in
307	  `prolog:prolog_exception_hook/5` (the exception is not changed, and the
308	  program's own `catch/3` of it is respected: only an exception that
309	  reaches the harness is reported);
310	- at the safety limit: the same, read by the harness's SIGUSR1 handler (§ 10);
311	- where the last request failed (exhausted): nothing is held, `raw` is
312	  empty, and `method` says so.
313	
314	`observe.bindings` splits the rendering by unknown (the toplevel's
315	`binding(Names, Value, _)` groups); an unknown that only has residual
316	goals has no entry. Beside it the harness reads `term_attvars/2` of the
317	unknowns and the number of `copy_term/3` residual goals (`suspended`), and
318	in storage mode the retained choicepoints and the store (§ 8).
319	
320	**print()** is the toplevel's transcript of the answers: each answer's
321	text, `;\n` between answers when another was requested, and `false.` when
322	the last request failed. For a session stage whose answers come from a
323	separate run, it is the rendering of what the incremental computation
324	holds.
325	
326	## 4. Execution state
327	
328	Per computation, after `answers()` (on the separate run, where answers
329	were taken there; `QUESTIONS.md`, Q14 of the common part), with `basis`:
330	
331	| state | when |
332	|---|---|
333	| `budget` | `inference_limit_exceeded` reached the harness (§ 9) |
334	| `error` | another exception reached the harness's `catch/3`; `error_verbatim` is SWI-Prolog's message for it, then `% term:` and the term |
335	| `timeout` | the safety limit stopped the attempt |
336	| `alternatives pending` | collection stopped at the cap with choicepoints newer than the query's mark (a request for more would resume it) |
337	| `suspended` | at the last answer, attributed variables are reachable from the unknowns (`term_attvars/2`: freeze, when, dif, clpfd, clpq goals held); or, in session, the computation waits in `h_wait/0` |
338	| `finished` | none of these: the goal exited without choicepoints and holds no attributed variable, or the last request failed |
339	
340	The incremental computation's own state, where answers came from a
341	separate run, is in the attempt's `notes`.

343	## 5. Steps (the H class's cost)
344	
345	The step is one inference (`statistics(inferences)`), as the systems file
346	qualifies it. **A program's steps are the inferences of its own goals**:
347	from the call of `stage(1, Vars)` to the end of the stage, every call and
348	redo port of the program's code (the program's S code included), and
349	none of the harness's: the stage marks, the answer points, observe(), the
350	H predicates (their call ports included), the storage sampler, the
351	exception hook. Each piece of harness code that runs inside the
352	computation runs *paused*: it reads the counter when it starts and when
353	it ends and adds what it spent, plus the few inferences around those two
354	readings, to an exclusion counter. The qualification shows that this is
355	exact: for made-up programs the steps the harness reports at the first
356	answer, at every answer and at the end equal the systems file's
357	measurement, the `statistics/2` difference minus one around the posed
358	goals (and, in *plain*, its other one, the smallest limit under which
359	`call_with_inference_limit/3` lets them reach that point; outside *plain*
360	the two differ, `QUESTIONS.md`, S16); behaviour, cost and storage runs report the
361	same steps; and a program with `h_count/1` calls has the same steps as
362	without them.
363	
364	Figures (`steps`): `restated`, the steps from the start of the run to the
365	end of the stage (for a reposed stage, the replay included); `restart_cost`,
366	for a reposed stage, the steps when stage k was first entered, after the
367	replay (`restart_cost_method: in-run`); `to_first_answer`, `steps_at`,
368	`between_answers` and `to_end` are counted **from the posing of stage k**
369	(after the replay; for an incremental stage, from the end of stage k−1);
370	`stage`, for an incremental stage, the steps from the end of stage k−1 to
371	the end of stage k. `repeated_work` is null: the systems file measures it
372	only by the program's problem-operation counters (`h_count/1`). Steps are
373	recorded in every mode; the figures of record are the cost run's.
374	
375	## 6. Modes
376	
377	| mode | instrumentation |
378	|---|---|
379	| behaviour | the budget counter and the stage marks only |
380	| cost | the same: step counting is the budget counter itself (`steps_at` at every answer) |
381	| storage | in addition: retained choicepoints at each answer, at the boundary and at the budget; the store vector at the boundary after `garbage_collect/0`; except in *tabling* (`QUESTIONS.md`, S17), a heartbeat sampler (`heartbeat` flag every 1008 inferences) keeping sampled maxima of choicepoints and global/local/trail use in `flag/3` |
382	
383	All storage-mode readings are paused, so storage steps equal behaviour
384	steps, but they move garbage collection, memory layout and where the
385	heartbeat falls, so the store is taken only from storage records and the
386	step count never from them. P13 records `cpu_time_s` and `max_rss_kb`
387	(the process's, from `wait4`) in behaviour and cost runs, where there is
388	one stage per process; null otherwise.
389	
390	## 7. Alternatives and suspended work
391	
392	`alternatives` is in the systems file's unit, **retained choicepoints**:
393	choicepoint frames newer than the mark taken where the computation's query
394	starts (so the harness's own frames are excluded), counted by walking
395	`prolog_choice_attribute/3`, by type, exactly as the systems file's probe
396	`cpcount.pl` does, at each answer before the next is requested
397	(`alternatives_at`), at the boundary, inside the exception hook when the
398	budget runs out (`at_budget`), and as a sampled maximum (`peak.kind:
399	sampled`, storage only). `held_as: backtracking`. After an exhausted query
400	none are held (`at_boundary: 0`). Problem-defined alternatives come from
401	`h_held/2`. `suspended`: attributed variables reachable from the unknowns
402	and residual goals, at the boundary, in every mode; in session an engine
403	waiting in `h_wait/0` is one item.
404	
405	## 8. Store
406	
407	Storage mode, at the stage boundary (where the computation still holds
408	its last answer, or after the query failed), after `garbage_collect/0`:
409	`global_live_bytes` (`statistics(globalused)`), `local_bytes`,
410	`trail_bytes`; *tabling*: `table_space_used_bytes`, `tables` and
411	`table_answers` (`current_table/2`, `trie_property/2`); *coroutines*,
412	*constraints*, *session*: `attributed_variables`, `residual_goals`. Each
413	with a sampled maximum where the sampler covers it (garbage included for
414	global; never called a peak), and the same quantities read before the
415	computation started (`*_at_computation_start`, the harness's baseline).
416	In session the store is the engine's own stacks.
417	
418	## 9. Budget
419	
420	10⁶ inferences per stage and computation (10⁸ for P12, P13, P16), from
421	`stages.json`; a reposed stage has its measured in-run restart cost plus
422	that. The budget is the system's inference limit, set absolutely with the
423	predicates `call_with_inference_limit/3` is built from
424	(`'$inference_limit'/2`, `'$inference_limit_false'/1`): that predicate
425	itself restarts its limit for every solution, so it cannot bound a stage
426	that collects several answers. Every stage mark's first entry gives its
427	stage the budget from there; every paused piece of harness code lifts
428	the limit on entry and puts it back, moved on by what it spent, on exit.
429	While program code runs the limit stands 8 inferences (the most any
430	harness entry spends before lifting it) beyond the program's budget, and
431	**every harness entry checks the budget exactly**: if the program's steps
432	exceed it, it raises `inference_limit_exceeded` itself. So a stage is
433	*budget* exactly when its program steps exceed its budget (the
434	qualification: 5000 steps finish under a budget of 5000, 5001 do not),
435	and between harness entries the system's limit stops it at most 8
436	inferences late (recorded in `restated`). A program's own `catch/3` with
437	a variable catcher can intercept the exception, as with
438	`call_with_inference_limit/3`.
439	
440	During a replay each replayed stage has the budget it had when first
441	posed. If the replay runs out of budget, or is stopped by the safety
442	limit, before stage k is posed, the restart cost is every step of the
443	replay, read when it stopped (`restart_cost_source` says so).
444	
445	**After budget: no configuration can continue.** The limit aborts the
446	stage's goal (the exception unwinds it), so the exhausted computation
447	cannot be resumed; stage k+1 is posed by reposing stages 1 … k+1
448	(`reason: after-budget`). After error and after timeout, likewise.
449	
450	## 10. Safety limit
451	
452	60 s per stage attempt (600 s for P12, P13, P16, fixed), from the
453	problem's limits; one rerun at 600 s where allowed. For a reposed stage it
454	covers the whole process (load, replay, stage); for an incremental stage,
455	from posting the stage to its end. The driver stops the system by sending
456	**SIGUSR1**: at the next point where the virtual machine handles signals,
457	the harness's handler reads the step count and the state held (the
458	observation recorded at the timeout), reports them, and ends the process
459	with SIGKILL; if the process has not ended 3 s later the driver sends
460	SIGKILL (`safety_limit.how_stopped` says which). The stopped computation
461	is gone, so the rerun is a reposed run of stages 1 … k (attempt 2,
462	`safety-rerun`), and after a final timeout stage k+1 is reposed
463	(`after-timeout`).
464	
465	## 11. Effects (P11)
466	
467	`emit(M)` writes the entry, flushed at once, to a spool file of the
468	process, with the stage being posed, the attempt, and `during_replay_of`
469	(the stage whose code is running, when it is earlier than the stage being
470	posed in a reposed run; null otherwise). When the attempt (or, in
471	session, the stage) ends, the driver appends the spool's entries, in
472	order, to the log, with `seq` and `run_id`: the classification log
473	`OUTDIR/<instance>.effects.jsonl` for behaviour runs, the observation log
474	`OUTDIR/<instance>.effects-observation.jsonl` for cost and storage runs
475	and separate runs. With `OUTDIR` as the common contract gives it
476	(`results/swi-prolog/<configuration>/P11/raw/`), these are the paths it
477	names. Logs are never reset. A commit stage's first answer, verbatim, is
478	kept and passed back, by `h_commitment/1`, whenever that stage is
479	replayed.
480	
481	## 12. H tokens
482	
483	A program's H constructs, class H in `METRICS.md`:
484	
485	- the heads of `unknowns/2`, `stage/3`, `query/2` and `spawned/4` clauses
486	  (the functor, the stage number or `_`, the computation id, the argument
487	  that receives the unknowns and the one that receives the constants:
488	  `stage(1, [A, _], Cs) :-` is H, with its `:-`), and the whole of each
489	  `unknowns/2` fact; the CONSTANTS block's markers and `% stage K` lines
490	  are comments;
491	- every call of `h_param/2`, `h_commitment/1`, `emit/1`, `h_count/1`,
492	  `h_candidate/0`, `h_held/2` and `h_wait/0`, with its arguments;
493	- output adapters (rule 13), if a program has any.
494	
495	A clause body of `stage/3` or `query/2`, and everything else, is classed
496	by `METRICS.md`'s rules. `S/session-wait.pl` is S (`S-mechanisms.md`).
497	
498	## 13. Confounds
499	
500	Everything the harness does beyond passing stages in, collecting answers
501	and reading state (also copied into every record's `run.confounds`):
502	
503	1. Stages are posed by calling the program's `stage/3` (with the constants
504	   of the stages posed so far) for stages 1..k and
505	   then `query/2` for k, as one conjunction compiled into one clause (the
506	   reposed configurations), or by posting each stage into one engine,
507	   whose loop is the harness's (session). A stage mark precedes each
508	   `stage/3` call; its inferences are excluded. The CONSTANTS block is
509	   blanked out of the text that is loaded, and its entries are passed in
510	   as `stage/3`'s last argument (§ 2.5).
511	2. Harness code inside the measured computation is excluded from the steps
512	   and the budget by moving the inference limit on by what it spent
513	   (SWI-Prolog internals `'$inference_limit'/2` and
514	   `'$inference_limit_false'/1`), and the budget is enforced with them, not
515	   with `call_with_inference_limit/3`, which restarts its limit per
516	   solution. Between harness entries the system's limit stands 8
517	   inferences beyond the budget.
518	3. Answers are rendered with the toplevel's own code, with
519	   `answer_write_options` `max_depth(0)` instead of `max_depth(10)`.
520	4. `autoload_all/0` after loading the program (the `autoload` flag is
521	   restored).
522	5. `prolog:prolog_exception_hook/5` reads the state when any exception is
523	   raised in the computation, before unwinding, and reports it if the
524	   exception reaches the harness. It does not change the exception.
525	6. observe() reads `term_attvars/2`, `copy_term/3` and the toplevel
526	   rendering at the end of the stage (and, storage, choicepoints and the
527	   store after `garbage_collect/0`).
528	7. Storage mode: a heartbeat sampler (`heartbeat` flag every 1008
529	   inferences), with `flag/3` maxima; excluded from steps, but it moves GC
530	   and layout.
531	8. One fresh `swipl` process per reposed stage attempt; one per session
532	   computation, and one per separate run.
533	9. Session: answers of a non-final stage on a separate run of 1..k.
534	10. Spawned computations as successive separate queries in one process.
535	11. The effects stub's entries go to a spool file and are appended to the
536	    log by the driver when the attempt ends.
537	12. Session only: the S code of `S/session-wait.pl` (an
538	    `user:exception/3` hook) is loaded before the program. It is part of the
539	    configuration as the systems file defines it, and is counted as S.
540	13. The safety limit is enforced by a SIGUSR1 handler of the harness,
541	    which reads the state and kills the process.
542	
543	## 14. check
544	
545	    harnesses/swi-prolog/check CONFIGURATION PROGRAM
546	
547	The same for every configuration, with configuration-specific warnings.
548	It **executes nothing of the program**: it reads the program's terms with
549	`read_term/3`, the reader the compiler uses, into a scratch module, and
550	
551	- reports syntax errors verbatim as SWI-Prolog's message system words
552	  them (`print_message/2`), and continues after each;
553	- never compiles or asserts a clause, never executes a directive, never
554	  calls a goal of the program, never poses a stage. Three kinds of
555	  directive are interpreted for their effect on reading only: `op/3`
556	  (applied to the scratch module), and `use_module/1,2`, `ensure_loaded/1`
557	  and `autoload/1,2` of `library(...)` (the library is loaded into the
558	  scratch module, so that its operators, such as clpfd's `#=`, and its
559	  exports are known: that runs the library's code, never the program's).
560	  `dynamic/1` and `table/1` are noted. Every other directive is listed as
561	  not executed;
562	- then checks statically: singleton variables (as the compiler would warn);
563	  calls to procedures that nothing defines (the program's clauses and
564	  dynamic declarations, built-ins, the loaded libraries, the autoload
565	  index, the H predicates), through the control constructs and the
566	  meta-calls whose argument is a goal; the contract (`unknowns/2`,
567	  `stage/3`, `query/2`, `spawned/4`); the `CONSTANTS` block's form (one
568	  pair of markers, `% stage K` sections in increasing order before any
569	  entry, facts only), whose entries are checked as entries and not counted
570	  as the program's clauses; the `PROVENANCE` comment; and mechanisms the
571	  configuration does not have (`:- table` outside *tabling*; `freeze/2`,
572	  `when/2`, `dif/2` outside *coroutines*, *constraints*, *session*;
573	  clpfd/clpq outside *constraints*, *session*; engines and `h_wait/0`
574	  outside *session*), as warnings.
575	
576	Exit status 0 when there is no error, 1 when there are errors (syntax
577	errors; neither `stage/3` nor `spawned/4`; `stage/3` without `query/2`;
578	a `stage/2` or `spawned/3`; a malformed CONSTANTS block), 2 usage. The qualification shows that a
579	program whose every directive and goal would print a marker and write a
580	file leaves no trace under `check`, and leaves both under `run`.
581	
582	## 15. Qualification
583	
584	[`qualification/`](qualification): made-up programs, a made-up stages file,
585	`run.py` (inside the image) and `rerun.sh` (from the host), its
586	`output.txt`, and every record it wrote, under `records/`.
587

content.content:
# Questions: the SWI-Prolog harness

*Where the common contract (`harnesses/README.md`, `harnesses/QUESTIONS.md`)
or the specification could not be implemented as written for SWI-Prolog,
or left a choice, and the reading implemented. No file outside
`harnesses/swi-prolog/` was changed. The common part's readings Q1–Q19
are implemented as written.*

## S1. The budget cannot be enforced with `call_with_inference_limit/3`

The systems file names `call_with_inference_limit/3` as the budget
mechanism. That predicate restarts its limit for each solution (on
backtracking into it, the limit is set again, in full), and it counts
whatever the harness does between answers against nothing; a stage that
collects several answers, or whose budget must be the restart cost plus
10⁶ from the start of a reposed run, cannot be bounded by it.

**Implemented:** the same limit, set absolutely with the predicates
`call_with_inference_limit/3` is built from (`'$inference_limit'/2` and
`'$inference_limit_false'/1`), raising the same `inference_limit_exceeded`.
Harness code inside the computation lifts it and puts it back, moved on
by what it spent, so that only the program's inferences count. Since
entering harness code costs a few inferences before the limit can be
lifted, the limit stands 8 inferences beyond the budget while program
code runs, and every harness entry checks the budget exactly, raising the
exception itself when the program's steps exceed it. So the *budget*
classification is exact at every harness entry (each answer, each stage
mark, each H call, the end of the stage); between harness entries the
system stops a stage at most 8 inferences after its budget, and the steps
recorded at that stop say so. Listed as a confound.

## S2. A replay that does not reach stage k

The in-run restart cost is "the step count at the moment stage k is first
posed". If the replay of stages 1 … k−1 runs out of a replayed stage's
budget, or is stopped by the safety limit, stage k is never posed.

**Implemented:** the restart cost is every step the replay took, read when
it stopped (in the exception hook, or by the SIGUSR1 handler), with
`restart_cost_method: in-run` and a `restart_cost_source` that says so;
the stage's budget is that plus 10⁶, and the stage is *budget* or
*timeout*. If the process ends at the safety limit without answering
SIGUSR1 (a loop inside a foreign predicate, which never reaches a point
where signals are handled), no count can be read; the restart cost is
then null, the record does not validate, and `run` keeps it as
`.INVALID.json` and exits 3, rather than estimate it.

## S3. A session computation that has failed cannot receive the next stage

In *session*, if the computation fails (a stage's goal and every earlier
alternative fail), the engine has finished: there is no computation to
post stage k+1 into, and none of the reasons of the record (`after-budget`,
`after-error`, `after-timeout`) applies.

**Implemented:** stage k+1 starts a new computation, with stages 1 … k
posted again (`posed.how = reposed`, `reason = configuration`), and the
stages after it are posted into that one. In a reposed configuration a
failed stage is followed the same way by every later stage.

## S4. Which session answers are taken on a separate run

The common contract: where collecting answers would consume the
computation the next stage extends, answers are taken on a separate run
of stages 1 … k.

**Implemented:** in *session*, at every stage except the instance's last,
`answers()` is taken on a separate run (a fresh process and engine:
stages 1 … k−1 posted as replay, then k with its query), and `observe()`
and `print()` read the incremental computation's held state without
consuming it (`taken_on: this-run`). At the instance's last stage nothing
extends the computation, so its answers are collected in it. A spawned
computation (P09) is likewise collected in place. The separate run's
`steps_restated` is beside the incremental stage's own steps; the
latencies (`to_first_answer`, `between_answers`, `to_end`) are the
separate run's, counted from the posing of stage k in it. `query(K, Vars)`
is called only where answers are collected, so in the incremental
computation it runs at the last stage only.

## S5. Spawned computations, and P16b

No SWI-Prolog configuration runs computations side by side by itself:
threads are in no configuration, and engines (in *session*) run only when
asked, so running them side by side would be the harness interleaving
them, which it may not do. Nor can separate computations share unknowns:
a separate query, an engine and a thread each copy their goal.

**Implemented:** a spawned computation is a separate query in the same
process, sharing its database, run to its end or budget before the next
(`side_by_side: false`), in every configuration. P16b is always posed by
its fallback, the four contributions as one conjunction in `main`.

## S6. After budget, no configuration can continue

The budget's exception unwinds the stage's goal, so the computation that
ran out cannot be resumed with a new budget in any configuration, *session*
included (the engine survives, but the stage's work is undone).

**Implemented:** stage k+1 after *budget* is reposed (`after-budget`) in
every configuration; `continued_after_budget` is never true.

## S7. What observe() reads when the answers are exhausted

When the last request for an answer fails, backtracking has left the
posed goal: no binding, choicepoint or attributed variable of it is held.

**Implemented:** `observe.raw` is empty and `method` says why; the answers
themselves are recorded verbatim. Where the query is still at an answer
(cap, or a last answer without choicepoints), at the budget, at an error
and at the safety limit, observe() reads the state held there.

## S8. H calls and the step count

`METRICS.md` classes the harness's calls as H tokens, and the steps are the
system's inferences.

**Implemented:** the inferences of H calls, their call ports included, are
excluded from the steps and from the budget, so that a program's steps
do not depend on whether it counts its problem operations, emits effects
or reads its parameters. A program's S code is not excluded.

## S9. Rendering answers

The toplevel elides answers deeper than `max_depth(10)`, which would lose
answers the classifiers need (long sequences, P13, P16).

**Implemented:** the toplevel's own rendering code with
`answer_write_options` `max_depth(0)`; otherwise as the toplevel prints.
A deterministic last answer ends `.` (the `query(yes(…))` message), a
nondeterministic one with a space (`query(more(…))`), exactly as the
toplevel prints them. A commit stage's value v is that text, verbatim,
trailing space or `.` included.

## S10. Where latency is counted from in a reposed stage

**Implemented:** `to_first_answer`, `steps_at`, `between_answers` and
`to_end` count from the posing of stage k, after the replay (so that
they are comparable with an incremental stage's); `restated` and
`restart_cost` give the run's totals.

## S11. The session configuration's supporting code

The systems file defines *session* as including "supporting code that
makes an application wait for an undefined procedure", counted as S, and
the S mechanisms must be listed with their size before any program is
run.

**Implemented:** that code is `S/session-wait.pl` (listed in
`S-mechanisms.md`), loaded by the harness in every *session* run before
the program. Its one call to the harness, `h_wait/0`, is H; the rest is S.
A *session* program may also wait explicitly with `h_wait/0`.

## S12. Messages that name the harness

SWI-Prolog's error messages include the predicate that called the failing
goal; where that is the clause the harness compiles for the query (last
call optimisation removes the program's frame), the message names
`'$cp_query'/1` (or, in *session*, `cp_harness:engine_step/4`), and under
`-g` the system prefixes `[Thread main]`.

**Implemented:** the message is recorded verbatim, as the system words
it.

## S13. `system_build`

The `swipl:11.0.1` image has no `/opt/src/COMMITS`, and a harness inside
the container cannot read the image's digest. **Implemented:** the build
is recorded as the pinned image's digest, `system_build.image`: the value
of `HARNESS_IMAGE_DIGEST` if the launcher sets it (else
`CP_IMAGE_DIGEST`), and otherwise the `swipl:11.0.1` index digest that
`PINS.md` pins,
`sha256:b51af487f3306fe240eae8c13159c85b5526509952e1b949cc22f48a1f82a742`.
`system_build.commit` stays null (there is no system commit for an image
pinned by digest), and `version_output` is `swipl --version`, verbatim.

## S14. The effects logs' folder

**Implemented:** the logs are written in `OUTDIR`, which for P11 is the
folder the common contract names (`results/swi-prolog/<configuration>/P11/raw/`);
the verifier's runs, under its own `OUTDIR`, have their own logs.

## S15. A separate run stopped by the safety limit

**Implemented:** the separate run of a *session* stage has the attempt's
limit; if it is stopped, the attempt is recorded as stopped by the
safety limit, and the stage is rerun as attempt 2 (a reposed run of
stages 1 … k under the raised limit), from which the incremental
computation continues.

## S16. The systems file's two step measurements do not always agree

The systems file says that the `statistics(inferences)` difference minus
one "is exactly the smallest limit `call_with_inference_limit/3` lets a
goal finish under". The qualification confirms it for some plain
programs (the probes, and made-up stages of facts and member/2), but finds
that it does not hold where coroutine wake-ups (freeze, dif, clpfd) or
tabling run, or memberchk/2 is called: there the smallest limit is smaller
(for a made-up clpfd stage, 100 against 111; for a tabled one, 4 against
63; for a stage that calls memberchk/2, a few inferences), presumably
because some of the work is not inside the limited call.

**Implemented:** the harness's steps are the `statistics/2` count, and its
budget is checked against that count at every harness entry (section 9),
so a stage's steps and its budget agree with each other and with the
`statistics/2` measurement in every configuration. The qualification
reports the `call_with_inference_limit/3` figure beside it, as
information. It also finds that the first call of a library predicate in
a process (memberchk/2 here) can cost an inference more than later calls,
so each `statistics/2` reference figure is taken first in a fresh
process, as the harness's are. The systems file's claim of agreement may
need an amendment.

## S17. No storage sampler in tabling

The heartbeat sampler's inferences are excluded from the steps like other
harness code; the qualification found that under tabling (SLG resolution,
which suspends and resumes goals with delimited continuations) this
exclusion is not exact (a made-up tabled stage gained 618 steps in its
storage run).

**Implemented:** in *tabling* the storage run takes no sampled maxima
(their `peak` is null); the store at the boundary, which tables only
grow, is still read. The other configurations sample as described.

## S18. No anticipation of constants (rule 5), made structural

A constants block loaded with the program would put every later stage's
constants into the system, as clauses, from stage 1 on, so that rule 5
would rest on the program's discipline alone.

**Implemented** (as for the other three systems): each entry of the block
is tagged by a `% stage K` comment line with the stage that first uses
it; the driver splits the block and loads the program with the block's
lines blanked; stage k's entries reach the process only when stage k is
posed, and the program only as the last argument of `stage(k, Vars,
Constants)`, the entries of stages 1 … k (again on every replay). The
program contract changes accordingly: `stage/3` and `spawned/4` replace
`stage/2` and `spawned/3`. The verifier still substitutes only the block.

One reading: in a reposed configuration a whole process poses stage k,
its replay of stages 1 … k−1 included, so stage k's entries are in that
process from its start (as text in the control file, read as terms when
the stage's goal is built). The replayed stages' code is called with only
the entries of their own stages 1 … j, so it cannot use them. In
*session*, stage k's entries arrive with the command that posts stage k.

The harness loads a stripped copy of the file (of the same name, in its
work directory), so that the system never opens the original; error
messages therefore name that copy's path, with the original's line
numbers.
# S mechanisms of the SWI-Prolog configurations

*`PROTOCOL.md`, "Recording a result": every configuration's S mechanisms
are listed, with their size, at phase 4, before any program is run.
`METRICS.md`, class S and rule 12: code that provides a mechanism the
configuration lacks, counted once per mechanism per configuration. This
file lists; it is not a problem program.*

The systems file (`systems/swi-prolog/README.md`, "Configurations")
admits supporting code in one configuration only: *session*, "with
supporting code that makes an application wait for an undefined
procedure", and says that it is counted as S there. The other four
configurations are defined by what SWI-Prolog itself provides, and name no
supporting code.

| configuration | S mechanisms the configuration provides | size |
|---|---|---|
| `plain` | none | — |
| `tabling` | none | — |
| `coroutines` | none | — |
| `constraints` | none | — |
| `session` | **wait for an undefined procedure**: [`S/session-wait.pl`](S/session-wait.pl) | 19 lines, 158 tokens (comments and layout not counted) |

## session: wait for an undefined procedure

[`S/session-wait.pl`](S/session-wait.pl), loaded by the harness before the
program in *session* only, so that it is part of every *session* run, as
the systems file defines the configuration. It is general over
procedures, not written for any problem.

When the session's computation (the engine that holds the stages) calls a
procedure that has no definition, SWI-Prolog consults the hook
`user:exception(undefined_predicate, PI, Action)` before raising the
existence error. The hook gives the procedure one waiting clause and
answers `retry`. The waiting clause waits, with the harness call
`h_wait/0` (class H: the stage ends with the computation waiting, and the
next stage is received into the same computation), until a stage has
given the procedure a clause of its own (by `assertz/1`); it then removes
itself and calls the procedure. Outside the session's engine (a spawned
computation runs as a separate query) the hook does nothing and the
system raises its error as usual. (The hook cannot wait itself, since it
is called from C, and an engine cannot yield from inside such a call;
hence the waiting clause.)

Its size: the file without its comments, 19 non-blank lines, 158 lexical
tokens (atoms, variables, numbers, strings, punctuation and operator
symbols), counted by a regular-expression tokeniser; the classifiers count
its tokens by `METRICS.md` themselves. Its inferences are the program's
(S code is not paused, unlike harness code).

A program may also write supporting code of its own, in any
configuration. That is the program's S, counted against that
configuration and listed by the classifiers (`METRICS.md`, rule 12), not a
mechanism the configuration provides.

## Not S

- The harness's predicates (`h_param/2`, `h_commitment/1`, `emit/1`,
  `h_count/1`, `h_candidate/0`, `h_held/2`, `h_wait/0`) are H
  (`README.md`, section 12).
- Libraries outside a configuration's core (`library(lists)`,
  `library(clpfd)`, …) are external mechanisms, listed under that metric,
  not S (`METRICS.md`, "The core of a configuration").
